title: What If a Whole Country Skipped a Day? Samoa Did
subject: Samoa calendar

scenes.text: What if a whole country skipped a day? Samoa did, and nobody got that Friday back.
At midnight on December 29, 2011, Samoa's calendar jumped from Thursday straight to Saturday.
Before that, when it was Friday in Samoa, it was already Saturday in New Zealand.
Its biggest trading partners were Australia and New Zealand, and the prime minister said Samoa was losing two working days a week.
The fix was crossing the International Date Line, which Samoa had crossed the other way in 1892 to match American trade.
That 1892 switch added a day instead, so Samoans celebrated two Fourths of July in a row.
